neighbours.label: the little word ('into', 'to', 'as') right after a verb and its object, where someone turns, makes or names that object into something new (verb + object + into/to/as + new state); not 'into' for motion, and not 'turned into' with no object in between
neighbours.short: into/to/as after verb + object: turning or naming it into something new
fire: The witch turned the prince into a frog with a single spell.
They elected her as chair of the committee last spring.
My grandmother made the old curtains into a quilt for the baby.
The committee named the new bridge as a memorial to the flood victims.
He converted the garage into a small recording studio.
Heat transforms the liquid water into steam within minutes.
The board appointed Lisa as the new treasurer.
She cut the dough into little star shapes for the party.
quiet: The witch walked the prince into the forest with a single lantern.
They elected her last spring, and she took the chair right away.
My grandmother carried the old curtains into the attic for storage.
The committee named the new bridge after a long debate.
He drove the car into the garage before the storm hit.
The liquid water slowly turned into steam within minutes.
The board thanked Lisa for her years of service.
She put the dough into the oven for the party.
